projects.name: Hangar
projects.tagline: Every Steam account, one click away.
projects.description: Switches the signed-in Steam account without the account picker or a password prompt, shows every game on every account, and brings your Steam friends, chat and profiles with it. Steam stays in the tray, holding a fraction of its usual memory in RAM.
highlights: Silent switching, straight to the tray
Play as… launches a game on the account that owns it
Your whole library, installed or not
Friends, chat and profiles, signed in with a QR code
Idle Steam holds 30–70 MB in RAM instead of about 330 MB
Never reads or stores passwords

engineering.title: Less RAM without breaking Steam
engineering.text: Launch flags barely help: the best set saved about 25 MB of Steam's ~330 MB, because most of it is a hidden web renderer every client keeps loaded. Instead, Hangar asks Windows to trim the working set of steam.exe and steamwebhelper (EmptyWorkingSet), a minute after Steam signs in and every five minutes after, never while a game is running. The working set is the part of a program's memory held in RAM. Idle in the tray, Steam's drops from about 330 MB to 30–70 MB, and it stays signed in. Steam's total allocated memory doesn't shrink: the trimmed pages wait in standby or the page file and come back if Steam touches them. Measured on Windows 11 with Steam signed in, idle in the tray and no game running.

engineering.title: No passwords, ever
engineering.text: Accounts connect with a QR code from the Steam Mobile App, so Hangar never sees a password. The sign-in token it gets back is stored encrypted with Windows DPAPI, readable only by your Windows account.

engineering.title: Its own line to Steam
engineering.text: Friends, chat and profiles run over Hangar's own connection to Steam's servers, so the Steam client stays signed in alongside it and games still launch through Steam as usual.

screenshots.alt: Home with a featured game, playtime and Continue Playing for the signed-in account.
Installed games in a grid of Steam cover art, with playtime for each.
Three remembered Steam accounts, each with a Switch button, and Add Account.

contacts: QR sign-in, your library, friends, chat, profiles and game artwork
only if you add your own key, to list games an account owns but hasn't played on this PC
to check for and download updates
local: Hangar never sees, reads or stores your Steam password
The sign-in token Steam gives Hangar is encrypted with Windows' own data protection (DPAPI), so only your Windows account can read it

projects.updates: Updates itself from its GitHub Releases page and checks each download against its SHA-256 hash before installing. You can turn this off under Settings › About.
requirements: The Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime, which comes with Windows 11
story: Steam keeps one account signed in at a time. Switching means opening its account picker and watching Steam restart in front of you, typing a password and a Steam Guard code for any account it has forgotten, and the library only shows the games of whoever is signed in. If the game you want is on your other account, you find out after the switch.

Hangar makes switching one click, shows every game on every account in one library, and switches for you when you press Play on a game another account owns. It does it with the sign-ins Steam already remembers, so it never needs your password.

projects.name: Verdant
projects.tagline: GeForce driver updates, without the NVIDIA App.
projects.description: Finds the latest Game Ready and Studio drivers for your NVIDIA card, checks they're signed by NVIDIA and installs them with one prompt, without the NVIDIA App.
highlights: Matches your exact card with NVIDIA's catalog
Only runs installers signed by NVIDIA
Never installs the NVIDIA App
Express or custom install, with roll back
Live GPU temperature, load and VRAM
Compact mode: a small window that keeps you current

engineering.title: Keeping the NVIDIA App out
engineering.text: Verdant unpacks NVIDIA's driver package itself and runs the installer from what's left. The NVIDIA App's folders are never extracted, any component the package marks as part of it is removed, and the install is refused if one remains. If NVIDIA's installer adds the app anyway, Verdant uninstalls it.

engineering.title: Only NVIDIA's own installers
engineering.text: Before anything runs, Verdant checks the driver installer is signed by NVIDIA and refuses it if not, so a tampered download never gets a chance to run.

screenshots.alt: Home with the latest Game Ready driver, 621.14, installed and up to date.
Every Game Ready driver for a GeForce RTX 2060, with the installed one marked and roll back for the rest.

contacts: your card's model, to find matching drivers, their release notes and the driver downloads
artwork for the games each driver is made for
to check for and download updates
local: Your GPU, driver version and live readings are read on your PC
Only installers signed by NVIDIA Corporation are run

projects.updates: Updates itself from its GitHub Releases page and checks each download against its SHA-256 hash before installing. You can turn this off under Settings › About.
requirements: The Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime, which comes with Windows 11
story: NVIDIA's own way to keep a GeForce driver current is the NVIDIA App, which installs its own overlay, background services and update checks alongside the driver. Most people only want the driver.
Verdant does that one job: it finds the right driver for your exact card, checks it really comes from NVIDIA, installs it with one prompt and keeps the NVIDIA App out.

projects.name: Keepsake
projects.tagline: Your emulator games and saves, in one place.
projects.description: Finds your RPCS3, Lichii and Fritchii games and every save, starts any game straight from its library, and edits the saves of supported games with each game's own artwork.
highlights: PS3, Switch and Switch 2 games in one library
Play without the emulator's game list
Save editors for three LEGO games and Ocarina of Time
Opens saves copied from a real PS3
Artwork from the eShop, Steam and SteamGridDB
A backup before every change

engineering.title: Saves from a real PS3
engineering.text: Saves copied off a PS3 are encrypted and signed. Keepsake decrypts them with each game's secure file ID and writes them back plain for RPCS3. Re-encrypting and re-signing is kept too, and tested against real saves.

engineering.title: Reading Switch 2 save data
engineering.text: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 stores its save in Nintendo's GameData format, where every field name is a MurmurHash3 hash. Keepsake maps those hashes to rupees, hearts, items, songs and more, per save slot, and keeps the save's caption file in sync.

engineering.title: The game's own icons
engineering.text: Switch games are encrypted, so Keepsake takes icons from the files your emulator already keeps: a game dump or a mod. It decodes the compressed archives and texture formats itself. Switch 2 lays texture bytes out differently from Switch 1, and that layout was worked out from real textures until every icon decoded cleanly.

projects.note: Not affiliated with the RPCS3, Lichii or Fritchii projects, Nintendo, Sony Interactive Entertainment, Warner Bros. Games, Disney, TT Games or the LEGO Group.

projects.updates: Updates itself from its GitHub Releases page and checks each download against its SHA-256 hash before installing. You can turn this off under Settings › About.
requirements: RPCS3, Lichii or Fritchii, with your own games
The Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime, which comes with Windows 11
story: Every emulator keeps its games and saves its own way, in its own folders, and editing a save usually means a hex editor and offsets copied from a forum post.

Keepsake puts the games and saves from RPCS3, Lichii and Fritchii in one library, starts any of them in one click, and turns supported saves into a form with the game's own artwork, with a backup before every change.

projects.name: Prism
projects.tagline: Colour profiles for every game, switched automatically.
projects.description: Gives every game its own vibrance, contrast and white balance, switched on when the game takes focus and off when you leave it. Works on any graphics card.
highlights: Switches with the game in focus, or while it runs
Vibrance up to 200%, past the driver
Contrast, brightness and white balance too
NVIDIA, AMD and Intel, no admin rights
Nothing injected into your games
About 4 MB of memory in the tray

engineering.title: Idle means idle
engineering.text: One engine thread owns the colour effect. It sleeps until Windows reports a new window in front, and only checks again while a profile needs it. Closing Prism's window destroys it and its web view entirely, so in the tray it uses about 4 MB and no CPU. That's its private memory as well as its working set (the part held in RAM), measured on Windows 11 with Prism idle in the tray.

engineering.title: Better than the original
engineering.text: Prism is a rewrite of Digital Vibrance in Rust. Along the way: the live preview no longer sticks on screen, a colour change Windows refuses is retried, and the list of running processes is no longer read every 1.5 seconds.

projects.note: Not affiliated with NVIDIA, AMD or Intel.

screenshots.alt: Home with FragPunk active in the top bar, its colours on screen, and every game profile.
Games in a grid, each with its own icon and vibrance.
Editing the Counter-Strike 2 profile: when it applies, vibrance at 200% with Override, contrast and brightness.

credits.name: Digital Vibrance
credits.text: Prism is a rewrite of Digital Vibrance in Rust, and imports its profiles.

contacts: to check for and download updates. Prism connects to nothing else
local: Prism watches which window is in front to switch profiles. That never leaves your PC
Nothing is injected into your games, and no admin rights are needed

projects.updates: Updates itself from its GitHub Releases page, also while it's in the tray, and checks each download against its SHA-256 hash before installing. You can turn this off under Settings › About.
requirements: Any NVIDIA, AMD or Intel graphics card
Games in borderless or windowed mode: exclusive fullscreen skips the effect, and HDR may change it
The Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime, which comes with Windows 11
story: Colour settings in a graphics driver are global. Turn vibrance up for one game and the desktop, every video and every other game change with it, so you end up flipping settings by hand each time you switch.

Prism gives each game its own colours and puts the desktop back the moment you leave the game. It began as Digital Vibrance, rewritten in Rust so it works the same on any graphics card and sits in the tray using almost nothing.

projects.name: Parley
projects.tagline: An unofficial, lightweight Discord client for Windows.
projects.description: A small native Discord client for Windows: servers, channels, DMs, replies, emoji and voice calls end-to-end encrypted with DAVE, Discord's own protocol for calls, in a single exe with no Electron and no browser engine. Text messages aren't end-to-end encrypted, in Parley or in any Discord client.
highlights: Servers, channels and DMs
Voice calls end-to-end encrypted with DAVE
Replies, emoji and invite cards
Sign in by scanning a QR code
Stays signed in across restarts
No Electron and no browser engine

engineering.title: Stays signed in
engineering.text: A failed first request after boot, before the network is up, no longer signs you out. Parley retries with backoff and only drops an account when Discord says its session is no longer valid. Saved accounts are written atomically, with a backup copy.

engineering.title: Lighter by subtraction
engineering.text: Screen sharing, camera, the bundled video library and the diagnostics tools were cut, taking the exe from 93 MB to 42 MB. With its window open and idle, Parley trims its own working set (the part of its memory held in RAM) to around 7 MB. The memory it has allocated in total is larger.

engineering.title: Careful updates
engineering.text: Parley updates itself from its GitHub releases and checks each download's SHA-256 hash first. It waits until you're not busy, gives you ten seconds to say Later, then updates quietly in the tray.

projects.note: Not made, approved or endorsed by Discord Inc.

screenshots.alt: A FragPunk server channel in Parley: the server and channel lists, messages with replies and emoji, and the message field. Names and avatars are blurred.
The same channel in Parley's light theme. Names and avatars are blurred.
Settings, Voice & Audio: output and input device, microphone gain and voice activity sensitivity.

warning.title: Unofficial client: use at your own risk
warning.text: Parley isn't made or approved by Discord. Discord's Terms of Service forbid “unauthorized software designed to modify the services”, and Discord can suspend or close accounts that break its terms. Discord can also change its service at any time, which may stop Parley working until it's updated. Screen sharing and camera aren't supported. Don't use it on an account you can't afford to lose.

credits.name: Litecord
credits.text: Parley began as Litecord. Its licence ships with Parley in the NOTICE file.

contacts: everything a Discord client does: sign-in, messages and voice
only if Discord asks for a captcha while you sign in
to check for and download updates
local: Your Discord session is encrypted with Windows' own data protection (DPAPI) and never leaves your PC except to talk to Discord
Voice calls are end-to-end encrypted with DAVE, Discord's protocol for calls. Text messages are encrypted on their way to Discord but not end to end, the same as in Discord's own app

projects.updates: Checks its GitHub Releases page for updates, verifies each download against its SHA-256 hash, and asks before installing.
requirements: A Discord account you're willing to risk (see the warning above)
WebView2, only for the captcha window
story: Discord's own app is built on Electron: a full copy of the Chromium browser, running in several processes even while it waits in the tray.

Parley does the everyday parts of Discord (servers, DMs and voice calls) in a small native exe instead. It says plainly what it leaves out and what using an unofficial client risks, so you can decide whether it's for you.
